## How the guide defines it

## How the guide uses it

On only 14 pages, which understates how contested it is. It appears mainly where a contributor is arguing *against* it: John McKechnie states plainly that roster continuity is overrated in this era because the elite programmes reload through the portal, and makes that the basis of a national-championship bet on Miami.

## Working definition — TTW DERIVED

How much of a roster — as opposed to a coaching staff — is unchanged from the previous season.

## Why it matters — TTW DERIVED

It is the concept the portal era has destabilised most, and the guide's contributors genuinely disagree about whether it still predicts anything.

## How bettors use it in this guide

Both as an asset and as a dismissal, in the same book. Makinen's transition systems treat returning starters as a hard threshold; McKechnie treats the same idea as outdated. Both positions are printed.
